answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can mandate slashable stake bonding, requiring nodes to lock capital in escrow before transacting. This imposes a verifiable financial cost per identity, preventing zero-cost replication. Whether controlling a sparrow drone, an autonomous ocean probe, or a node in a compute nebula, agents forfeit their deposit upon provable misbehavior. However, this mechanism inherently privileges wealthy actors over resource-constrained agents.
